headline: Every byte input across the toolkit accepts any BufferSource: an ArrayBuffer, a DataView, or any typed array, not only a Buffer or a Uint8Array.
summary: The parsing, signing, and verifying verbs read their byte inputs from any BufferSource. A certificate or request DER, a message imprint, a nonce, a key identifier, a CSR, an HTTP request body, and the other byte-valued options may each be a `Buffer`, a `Uint8Array`, an `ArrayBuffer`, a `DataView`, or any other typed array, and every form is read the same way and produces the same result. The `Buffer` and `Uint8Array` inputs already accepted are unchanged, so no existing call needs to change; the wider forms are additive. Private keys, passwords, and other secret inputs keep their existing narrower contract. Two character-scanning string predicates are also exported: `pki.oid.isDottedDecimal` and `pki.asn1.isPrintableString`.

Added: Every byte-valued input accepts any `BufferSource`, not only a `Buffer` or a `Uint8Array`. This covers the parse verbs such as `pki.x509.parse` and `pki.pkcs8.parse`; the certificate, request, and DER inputs to the signing and verifying verbs; a `messageImprint` in `pki.tsp.sign` and `pki.tsp.verify`; an OCSP `requestorName` and nonce; a CMP `expectedSender` and signer certificate; a CMC signer's `keyIdentifier` and `spki`; an EST enrollment CSR; a `subjectKeyIdentifier` or `authorityKeyIdentifier` key id; an `initialPermittedSubtrees` or `initialExcludedSubtrees` `iPAddress` base in `pki.path.validate`; and an HTTP request body. An `ArrayBuffer` or a `DataView` produces the same result as the equivalent `Buffer`.
`pki.oid.isDottedDecimal(s)` reports whether a string is a dotted-decimal object identifier: two or more numeric arcs separated by dots.
`pki.asn1.isPrintableString(s)` reports whether a string contains only the characters an ASN.1 PrintableString may carry: `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, space, and the symbols `'()+,-./:=?`.
Changed: A private key, a password, and other secret byte inputs keep their existing contract of a `Buffer`, a `Uint8Array`, a PEM string, or a `CryptoKey` where one is accepted. A secret input still refuses an `ArrayBuffer` with a typed error, because widening the secret ownership paths is a separate decision.
